title: Represent Fractions on a Number Line
goal: I can count equal intervals from 0 to name a fraction point between 0 and 1.
catchAll: The distance from 0 to 1 is one whole. Count spaces for the bottom, then spaces from 0 to the point for the top.

teacher.def: The denominator of a fraction tells how many equal parts are in the whole. It is the bottom part of the fraction
A unit fraction is ONE part of a whole. It always has a numerator of one.
The numerator of a fraction tells how many equal parts are being described. It is the top part of the fraction.
A fraction is a number used when a whole is split into equal parts.

glossary.whole: the distance from 0 to 1 on this number line
glossary.interval: a space between neighboring tick marks
glossary.tick: a mark that shows an interval boundary
glossary.denominator: number of equal intervals in one whole
glossary.numerator: number of equal intervals from 0 to the named point

screens.title: A whole can be a distance
text: Here 0 is the start and 1 is one whole away.
The dot starts at 0.

screens.title: Divide the distance equally
text: The distance from 0 to 1 has four equal spaces.
Each space is an interval; the bottom count is 4.

screens.title: Take one equal step
text: Move from 0 across one space.
The point is at 1/4. Do not count the 0 tick as a step.

screens.title: Keep counting spaces
text: The point has moved across three spaces from 0.
Three of the four equal intervals is 3/4.

screens.title: Ticks are boundaries, not parts
text: This unit has four spaces but five tick marks.
The four spaces partition the distance, so the denominator is 4.

screens.title: Start with a familiar strip
text: This strip has three equal pieces.
One selected piece is 1/3 of the whole.

screens.title: Now use a distance instead
text: This line also divides one whole into thirds.
One equal interval reaches 1/3; the whole is the distance from 0 to 1.
